stillSvg, figureStillSvg, gelStillSvg and plateStillSvg return an object with the keys svg, hidden and notice, as the file SVG calls do. It has no pages.

The SVG has the same layout as the file SVG. Each text is a <text> element, and each hover is a <title>. These calls need only the viewer. Their SVG draws in the viewer's fonts only on a page that holds the font rules, from fontRules or declareFaces.

Each throws as the file SVG calls do.

items.title: Hidden labels
items.text:
Each item of hidden is one label left out because it would overlap. It names the thing the label belongs to and gives its spans or its point, in the record's own numbers.

Key Type What it holds kind string "features", "primers", "cuts", "insertions", "reads" or "disagreements". name string The thing's name. A cut site's name is its enzymes' names, as in BanII - SacI. spans array of {start, end} The spans of a feature, a primer site, a read or a disagreement over a span. at number The point of a cut site, an insertion or a disagreement at a point.

Each item has either spans or at, never both.

items.title: fontRules
items.text:
molviz.fontRules()

Returns the font rules as CSS text: one @font-face rule for each of the viewer's fonts. Each rule loads its font from a data URL, so the page needs no network. A page writes the rules once, in a <style> element, for every still SVG it holds. Python's font_rules() returns the same text.

items.title: declareFaces
items.text:
molviz.declareFaces(document)

Adds the font rules to document once, as a <style id="molviz-fonts"> element at the end of its <head>. A second call finds that element and does nothing. Returns undefined.

Every draw call calls it.

items.title: calls
items.text:
An object that names each input's four calls, so code can pick a call by the input's name. Its keys are record, figure, gel and plate. Each value is an object with the keys check, draw, svg and still, whose values are names on molviz.

const call = molviz.calls.gel.draw; // "drawGel"
molviz[call](element, gel);

items.title: SEQUENCE_VIEW_LIMIT
items.text: The number 100000: the most bases of a span that the sequence view draws. Python's SEQUENCE_VIEW_LIMIT is the same number.

items.title: FormatError
items.text:
The error a call throws when an input or its options break the format. It is an Error whose name is "FormatError". The class itself is not on molviz, so code tells the error apart by its name.

Its message names every problem by its path, one problem to a line. A problem in the options has a path that starts with options, and a problem in a figure's list has one that starts with records. For example:

  • A record whose bases hold an X: bases: has "X" at index 3, which is not an IUPAC nucleotide letter.
  • A highlight that names nothing in the record: options.highlight[0]: names nothing in the record.
  • A figure with no records: records: must hold at least one record.

items.title: Plate format
items.text:
A plate is a grid of wells in rows and columns, with what each well holds. It holds no record. In Python a plate is a dict, which molviz.check_plate checks and molviz.draw_plate draws. In a page it is a JSON object, which the global molviz.checkPlate checks and molviz.drawPlate draws. Both run the same check.

The check reports every problem it finds, each named by its path, such as wells.I1: not on the plate, which runs A1 to H12. Python raises ValueError, and the page's check throws a FormatError. A key that is not on this page is an error. The types are the ones on the record format page.

Draw a plate and a stamp writes plates in this format, a stamp among them, and draws them.

items.title: Example
items.text:
This 96-well plate holds three clones in its first row and water in its last well.

{
  "title": "Colony picks",
  "rows": 8,
  "columns": 12,
  "wells": {
    "A1": "clone 1",
    "A2": "clone 2",
    "A3": "clone 3",
    "H12": "water"
  }
}

items.title: The plate
items.text:
Key Type Required Default Meaning title text no none The title drawn over the plate. A page written from the plate takes it as the page's title, or "Plate" when there is none. rows integer, 1 or more yes How many rows the plate has, lettered from A at the top. columns integer, 1 or more yes How many columns it has, numbered from 1 at the left. wells wells no every well empty What each well holds, by the well's name.

Common plates have these sizes.

Plate rows columns Last well 96 wells 8 12 H12 384 wells 16 24 P24 1,536 wells 32 48 AF48

items.title: Wells
items.text:
wells is an object. Each key names a well, and its value is what the well holds.

Part Type Meaning key text A well's name: its row's letters, then its column's number, such as B3. The rows after Z are AA, AB and on. The letters are capitals and the number has no leading zero. The well is on the plate. value text, not blank What the well holds, such as a sample's name. Wells with the same text hold the same contents.

A well that is not in wells is empty and drawn grey.

items.title: Colours and the legend
items.text: Each different contents takes a colour, given out in reading order: across the first row, then the next. A legend under the plate gives each colour's contents. A plate with more than ten different contents draws every well that holds something in one colour, and its legend has one line that gives the count, such as 11 different contents, all one colour.

items.title: Stamps
items.text: The format has no stamp. A stamp's drawing is two plates: the plate it takes from and the plate it fills. Draw a stamp as two plates builds them.

items.title: Record format
items.text:
A record is one DNA molecule as you hand it to molviz: its name, whether it is circular, its bases, and what is drawn on it. In Python a record is a dict, which molviz.check checks and molviz.draw draws. In a page it is a JSON object, which the global molviz.check checks and molviz.draw draws. Both run the same check.

The check reports every problem it finds, each named by its path, such as features[0].segments[0].end: must be greater than start. Python raises ValueError, and the page's check throws a FormatError. A key that is not on this page is an error.

The guides Choose what a map shows, Show the bases, Check a clone against its reads and Stack records into a figure draw records in this format.

items.title: Example
items.text:
This circular record has one feature, one primer and two cuts.

{
  "name": "pDemo",
  "circular": true,
  "bases": "GAATTCATGAGCAAAGGCGAAGAACTGTTTACCGGCTAAGGATCCAAA",
  "features": [
    {
      "name": "ORF",
      "type": "CDS",
      "strand": 1,
      "segments": [{"start": 6, "end": 39}],
      "translation": "MSKGEELFTG*"
    }
  ],
  "primers": [
    {
      "name": "ORF forward",
      "bases": "GCGCATGAGCAAAGGCGAAGAACTG",
      "sites": [{"start": 6, "end": 27, "strand": 1}]
    }
  ],
  "cuts": [
    {"enzyme": "EcoRI", "start": 0, "end": 6, "at": 1, "stagger": 4},
    {"enzyme": "BamHI", "start": 39, "end": 45, "at": 40, "stagger": 4}
  ]
}

items.title: Types
items.text:
The tables on this page and the gel, plate and figure pages use these types.

Type In JSON In Python text a string str integer a number with no fraction int number a finite number int or float true or false true or false True or False list an array list object an object dict bases a string of IUPAC nucleotide letters, ACGTURYSWKMBDHVN, in either case str colour a string written #rrggbb, its digits in either case str

items.title: The record
items.text: Key Type Required Default Meaning name text yes The record's name. The map writes it with the record's length, in the circle's centre or under the line. circular true or false yes Whether the record is circular. Only a circular record can be drawn as a circle, and only its spans can run across the origin. bases bases, at least one yes The top strand, 5' to 3'. Its length is the record's length. features list of features no [] The named stretches of the record, such as a CDS or a promoter. primers list of primers no [] The primers, each drawn at every site it binds. cuts list of cuts no [] One item for each enzyme cutting at one place. molviz draws only the cuts listed here. insertions list of insertions no [] Points where bases are added. reads list of reads no [] The reads, each drawn over the bases it trusts. No two reads share a name. disagreements list of disagreements no [] Places where the reads differ from the record. tracks list of tracks no [] Curves sampled along the bases, such as a Sanger trace.

items.title: Features
items.text:
Each item of features is an object with these keys.

Key Type Required Default Meaning name text yes The feature's label. type text yes Its type, such as CDS or promoter. Any text is allowed. The type sets the default colour, and the types_off option names types. strand 1, -1, 0 or 2 yes 1 is the top strand and -1 the bottom strand. 0 is no strand, drawn with no arrowhead. 2 is both strands, drawn with an arrowhead at each end. segments list of segments, at least one yes The stretches the feature covers, joined in order. color colour no its type's colour The fill of each segment that has no colour of its own. translation text of capital letters and *, at least one no none The amino acids of a coding feature, one letter for each codon and * for a stop. The sequence view draws them over their codons. molviz does not translate. codon_start 1, 2 or 3 no 1 The base of the segments, counted from 1, that starts the first codon. Allowed only with translation.

A translation fits its segments. Three bases for each letter must fit in the bases the segments hold, counted from codon_start.

items.title: Segments
items.text:
Each item of segments is an object with these keys.

Key Type Required Default Meaning start integer yes The segment's first base. end integer yes The base after its last base. It is greater than start. color colour no the feature's colour This segment's fill.

The segments of a feature run in ascending order of start. The segment rules under Coordinates give the exceptions at the origin and at a linear record's end.

items.title: Colours by type
items.text:
A feature with no color takes its type's colour. A type matches only as written, in its case.

Colour Types #77aadd CDS, gene, mat_peptide, sig_peptide, transit_peptide, propeptide, proprotein, exon, C_region, D_segment, J_segment, N_region, S_region, V_region, V_segment #ee8866 promoter, enhancer, RBS, -10_signal, -35_signal, CAAT_signal, TATA_signal, GC_signal, attenuator, misc_signal, 5'UTR, regulatory #ffaabb terminator, polyA_signal, polyA_site, 3'UTR #eedd88 rep_origin, oriT #99ddff protein_bind, misc_binding #44bb99 ncRNA, misc_RNA, mRNA, tRNA, rRNA, tmRNA, precursor_RNA, prim_transcript #bbcc33 LTR, repeat_region, mobile_element, misc_recomb, stem_loop, D-loop #aa3377 primer_bind #dddddd any other type

items.title: Primers
items.text:
Each item of primers is an object with these keys.

Key Type Required Default Meaning name text yes The primer's label. bases bases, at least one yes The whole primer, 5' to 3'. Its last bases pair with the record at each site. The bases before them are its 5' tail. sites list of sites yes Each place the primer binds. The list may be empty.

items.title: Sites
items.text:
Each item of sites is an object with these keys. A site covers only the bases that pair, so it holds at most as many bases as the primer.

Key Type Required Default Meaning start integer yes The site's first base. end integer yes The base after its last base. It is greater than start, and end - start is at most the primer's length. strand 1 or -1 yes The strand whose bases the primer's bases match, read 5' to 3'. 1 is the top strand and -1 the bottom strand. mismatches list of integers no none The bases inside the site that the primer does not pair with, each a base of the record.

items.title: Cuts
items.text:
Each item of cuts is one enzyme cutting the record once, at one place. Two enzymes that cut at one place are two items.

Key Type Required Default Meaning enzyme text yes The enzyme's name. The enzymes and highlight options match it in any case. start integer yes The first base the enzyme recognises. end integer yes The base after the last base it recognises. It is greater than start. at integer yes The point where the top strand is cut. It may lie outside the recognised bases, as it does for an enzyme that cuts away from its site. stagger integer yes How far the bottom-strand cut lies from at. The bottom strand is cut at at + stagger. 0 is a blunt cut. A positive stagger leaves a 5' overhang, and a negative one a 3' overhang.

On a linear record, at + stagger is from 0 to the record's length.

items.title: Insertions
items.text:
Each item of insertions is an object with these keys.

Key Type Required Default Meaning name text yes The insertion's label. at integer yes The point where the bases go in. length integer, 1 or more yes How many bases go in. color colour no #cc3311 The colour of its mark and its label.

items.title: Reads
items.text:
Each item of reads is an object with these keys.

Key Type Required Default Meaning name text yes The read's label. No other read has this name. A disagreement names its reads by it. start integer yes The first base the read trusts. end integer yes The base after the last base it trusts. It is greater than start. strand 1 or -1 yes The strand the read runs along. 1 is the top strand and -1 the bottom strand.

items.title: Disagreements
items.text:
Each item of disagreements is an object with these keys. A disagreement lies either over a span, given by start and end, or at a point, given by at.

Key Type Required Default Meaning name text yes Its label, as your code writes it, such as 696 A>G. start integer with end, or else at The first base the reads differ at. end integer with start, or else at The base after the last base they differ at. It is greater than start. at integer without start and end The point where the reads hold bases the record lacks. bases bases yes What the reads hold there. Over a span, "" is a deletion. At a point, it holds at least one base. reads list of text yes The names of the reads that differ, each the name of a read in reads. color colour no #bbbbbb The colour of its bar, its mark and its label.

pUC19-GFP's verification record holds one read and two disagreements, each a single base:

{
  "reads": [
    {"name": "consensus.fasta", "start": 0, "end": 3347, "strand": 1}
  ],
  "disagreements": [
    {"name": "696 A>G", "start": 695, "end": 696, "bases": "G", "reads": ["consensus.fasta"], "color": "#cc3311"},
    {"name": "2687 C>T", "start": 2686, "end": 2687, "bases": "T", "reads": ["consensus.fasta"], "color": "#bbbbbb"}
  ]
}

items.title: Tracks
items.text:
Each item of tracks is a set of named curves sampled alike along the bases, such as the four channels of a Sanger trace. A sample is one point along the curves, and each curve holds one number for each sample. The sequence view draws each track under the rows its peaks reach.

Key Type Required Default Meaning name text yes The track's label. curves object of curves yes One curve for each base letter. peaks list of pairs of integers yes Each pair is [sample, base]: a sample's index, from 0, and the base of the record it lies over. The samples ascend, and each is less than the curves' length. The bases may descend, as they do for a read on the bottom strand.

items.title: Curves
items.text:
curves is an object with these keys.

Key Type Required Default Meaning A list of numbers yes The A channel's height at each sample. C list of numbers yes The C channel's, as long as A. G list of numbers yes The G channel's, as long as A. T list of numbers yes The T channel's, as long as A.

items.title: Coordinates
items.text: Every position in a record counts the top strand's bases from 0. A position is one of three things: a base, a span or a point between bases.

items.title: A base
items.text: A base is its index. The first base is 0, and the last is the record's length minus 1. A primer's mismatches and a track's peaks name bases.

items.title: A span
items.text:
A span is a start and an end. It holds the bases from start to end - 1. The base at end is not part of it and is not drawn. start is less than end, so a span holds at least one base. On a linear record, end is at most the record's length.

A feature's segments, a primer's sites, a cut's recognised bases, a read, a disagreement over a span and the span option are spans.

items.title: A point between bases
items.text:
A point is the number of bases before it. A cut after the 406th base is at 406. On a linear record a point is from 0 to the record's length. On a circular record the origin is 0, never the length, so a point is from 0 to the length minus 1.

A cut's at, an insertion's at and a disagreement's at are points.

items.title: Across the origin
items.text:
On a circular record a span may run across the origin. Its end then passes the record's length, and the bases past the length count on from 0. A span runs at most one turn, so end - start is at most the length.

pUC19-GFP has 3,347 bases. Its BsmBI site has start 3343 and end 3349, so it holds bases 3343 to 3346 and then 0 to 1. Its top-strand cut, after the record's third base, is at 3 and never 3350.

items.title: A feature's segments
items.text:
A feature's segments run in ascending order of start, with two exceptions.

  • On a circular record, a later segment may start past the length, counted on across the origin. Every segment ends at most one turn past the first segment's start.
  • On a linear record, a feature may run off the record's end and on from its start, once. One segment then starts lower than the one before it, and the segments after it ascend again. Each segment from that one on ends at or before the first segment's start. In the pUC19 backbone amplicon, a linear record of 2,662 bases, lacZα has the segments {"start": 2394, "end": 2644} and then {"start": 14, "end": 32}.
